texts: Marfan syndrome is best confirmed, under the revised Ghent criteria, by a family history of Marfan syndrome together with a dilated aortic root, with a Z-score of 2 or more in adults or 3 or more under 20.
Her root of 4.5 cm with a Z-score of 3.5 and an affected parent meet the criteria.
A positive FBN1 test alone is not enough without an aortic or systemic feature, and many FBN1 variants are of uncertain meaning.
A bifid uvula points to Loeys-Dietz syndrome, and a pectus excavatum adds only one or two points to the systemic score.
In the picture, the young marionette hangs beside her parent on one family tree while the zebra measures her jar against the normal ones.
Memory hook: one family tree and a zebra's measure confirm Marfan.
